newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates fall on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates fall on rate cut.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates fell two points on Thursday, in line with this morning's cut in the Central Bank overnight interest rates, traders said.
Interbank rates were down to an average of 18.03125 percent from 20.03125.
The cuts, however, failed to convince some banks that the foreign exchange market was normalising and they refrained from taking positions in the secondary market.
In an interview with Reuters earlier, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said rates could return to normal next week if conditions were right.
Some banks believe rates are now headed downwards, while others continue to be wary, dealers said.
"It (the speculation) may not yet be over. It's not just us. It's all over the region," a dealer said.
The Philippine Central Bank had to raise its overnight borrowing by 8.75 percentage points last week to protect the peso against speculation caused by the turmoil in the Thai baht.
Done rates at the interbank call loan market was from 18.25 percent to 18.03125, with 30 lenders and 16 borrowers. Volume was lower at 13.55 billion from 14.26 billion pesos.
A Reuter poll of six financial institutions gave bid rates of 10.925/11.25 percent and offers of 10.85/11 percent for the three-month bills.
